top_choice_rationale: P001 (Chetty, Hendren, Friedman) ranks first on one common weighting of identification quality, conceptual originality, maturity and attribution tractability. It created a new empirical object, place-level mobility measured on population records. Its mover and childhood-exposure designs are explicit and large-sample, so outside researchers can probe them. The trio is the most tractable attribution among the proposals, though the Katz question remains a real judgement call. Maturity is its main weakness, since the core work dates from about 2014-2022 and long-run causal place-effect claims are still contested. The citation should therefore be limited to the measurement advance and the exposure-based designs, with no claim about long-run causal effects or policy prescriptions. P003 is second because of its maturity and concentrated credit, but its cross-country identification is weaker. P002 is third because it has the cleanest attribution and three decades of testing, but its aggregate evidence is mostly indirect and it overlaps with the 2022 prize. P004 is fourth because an eight-name field cannot be cut to three names on a defensible criterion. Each award proposal is still preferred to no award (P000).
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. None of Chetty, Hendren, Friedman, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Kiyotaki, Moore, Calvo, Taylor or Woodford appears among her listed co-authors or networks. Disclosed for context only: main co-author Magnus Johannesson was a committee member in 2016-19, she co-authored with former chair Tore Ellingsen in 2009, and her preference for transparent, checkable designs may favour P001. Not adjudicated.
